item.content:encoded:
The observation that two SCPs both into winter does not justify a whole paragraph of text. Two options would work better, both centering on this sentence:

Once SCP-2082's effect has covered an area greater than 20 square meters, the area around it will exude large amounts of ice and sleet from all solid surfaces.

The first is to hyperlink "exude large amounts of ice and sleet" straight to 2082. The second is to edit it to read:

Once SCP-2082's effect has covered an area greater than 20 square meters, the area around it will exude large amounts of ice and sleet from all solid surfaces in a manner similar to SCP-2082.

Really, the crosslinks strong enough to carry a paragraph of text by themselves are few and far between, and in those cases they're usually better-served by actually writing out the crosstest the paragraph usually suggests.

So here we have a matchbox that causes winter. There is another SCP object, one also written by Roget no less, with a similar effect to be found in SCP-2082, in which we have a extinct species of mammoth that cause the surrounding environment to drop in temperature/become winter. It may be possible that what ever gave 2082 its anomalous abilites may also be what 649 taps into. As such, I am proposing the following additional addendum:

Addendum 649-B: It is possible that the same anomalous effect that was historically responsible for SCP-2082 may be responsible for the effects observed during SCP-649 activation. Research into this hypothesis is currently underway using preserved SCP-2082 tissue samples. Proposals to resume SCP-2082 cloning to allow access to a live specimen have been denied.

In addition, an inline link to the Site-77 Dossier is recommended during its mention in the containment procedures.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm a very new SCP member, so I don't feel qualified to vote on any SCPs just yet.

However, I would like to make a comment on this SCP. I found the following to be quite noteworthy:

After one hour and forty five minutes(1:45:00), children's laughing could be heard, and a snowball hit Dr. Pena. Silhouettes of small forms could be seen through the fugue. Three (3) D-Class personnel were sent to investigate. When they did not return after an additional twenty (20) minutes, SCP-649 was closed and containment protocol initiated. The D-Class personnel have not been recovered. When the tape was replayed, one of the D-Class could be seen led by small figures through the walls of the test chamber. Records on the missing personnel indicate all three (one (1) male, two (2) female) had had children who had died before adolescence. All testing with such personnel has been suspended.

This is a very strange set of events: spectral "children" are seen, a real snowball materialises, and personnel disappear through solid walls. Surely these events would warrant further investigation?

Most strange of all, though, is how very unlikely it would be that all three personnel sent to investigate "…had had children who had died before adolescence", unless they had been selected according to that criterion - which, it is implied, was not the case. To lose a young child is very rare in the Western world, and I would say that it would be extremely unlikely to happen by pure chance that all three members of a group of test personnel would have lost a child.

In my view, when taken on its own, this apparently significant aspect of the test personnel serves to enhance, rather than detract from, the intrigue value of the SCP's effects. What spoils it for me is that the Foundation seems not to pick up on this notable piece of data, apart from, rather disappointingly, simply suspending all testing with "such personnel".

I would like to see some further extrapolation of this potentially novel idea: for example, what would happen if personnel who had not suffered the loss of a child entered the SCP's area of effect, and/or personnel who had lost a child, but at a post-adolescent age?

Certainly an aspect of the SCP's description which would benefit, I feel, from further development.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I find your new image to be both well-executed and realistic, and also far more suitable than the current one, for several reasons:

+ show block
– hide block

1. Although the text states that the SCP has "…the standard thirty two (32) match count", it makes no mention of the matchbox ever having actually contained any matches, and in fact goes so far as to state (via the footnote) the complete opposite, i.e. that the box "… contains no matches". This is completely inconsistent with the current image.

NB: One could simply assume that the matches had been removed at some point, but if so, one would also expect information to be provided as to why, when, by whom, for what reason, with what result, etc. The caption states that the image references "Documentation of SCP-649, prior to initial containment", but this just raises further problems: as pointed out by ZakMarcus later in this thread, there is no mention made of who documented the SCP before the Foundation, nor of what their findings were. This would presumably be important and relevant information, so its omission is notable.

2. The current image shows a matchbox with a capacity far smaller than that stated. I can count ~16 matches, and the box appears to be more or less completely full. A small niggle, but still, another inconsistency.

3. Although the text states that the only way to negate the effects of the SCP is to close the matchbox lid, the image shows a matchbox with no lid - just the inner tray.

4. The colour of the matches is unusual, yet no mention is made of this, nor of any investigations as to whether the unusual colour might be related to the SCP's effects.

5. The current image, colour-saturated and with no visible background, looks far too much like an enhanced and/or advertising image. Your image, showing the SCP at the point of its retrieval, is far more convincing; it looks like a real-world photograph, and also places the SCP very nicely in the context of its described effects.

Overall, in my view, replacing the current counter-intuitive image (and its problematic caption) with your image would greatly improve the overall impression this SCP makes upon the reader, both visually conveying its effects and adding significantly to its credibility.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Gonna critique the revisions, in case they get brought back, as they have the original author's stamp. (Though Roget's rewrite saved this from deletion, so authorship is now somewhat fuzzy.)

**Why not downgrade this SCP to safe? It doesn't seem to do anything unless opened, and the effects are relatively benign. I just see no reason to classify it euclid. ~ Dr. ██████ Pena

Sounds fine, I suppose, though unnecessary, and the formatting & caps errors need fixin'.

Addendum 649-B: On ██/██/20██, Doctor Pena, along with two D-Class Personnel vanished into the epicenter under blizzard conditions. All other researchers within 30 meters of the edge of SCP-649's effect reported small shadows barely in view, the sounds of children's laughter, and reported a pair of children's mittens after SCP-649's effect had subsided . The laughter was reported to have lasted from stage 3 until the weather effect ended, growing more distant as the effect receded. The mittens appear to be [DATA EXPUNGED].

I like this! Except for one thing…

…the last line is fucking terrible. You can't just do random frikkin expungement. "The mittens appear to be [SOFT AND WHITE]." "The mittens appear to be [KETER DICKS]." "The mittens appear to be [NAZI PARAPHENALIA]." "The mittens appear to be [SUPER SCARY OH MY GOD YOU GUYS.]" See how I can just fill in the blank with ludicrous stuff there and it all makes the same amount of sense? Expungement in this case should be an exercise in implication. We should have some idea of what the mittens are, or just friggin' tell us. Srsly.
